title: The Man, His Son, and His Donkey
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 父子俩听谁的话就改怎么骑驴，最后把驴扛起来，成了笑柄。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: A MAN and his Son were once driving their Donkey along a country road, to sell him at the fair. They soon passed some girls, who were drawing water at a well.
paragraphs.zh: 有一次，一个人带着儿子，赶着他们的驴子沿乡间大路走去，打算到集市上把驴卖掉。他们很快就经过一些在井边打水的姑娘。

paragraphs.en: “Look,” said one of the girls; “see those silly people trudging along in the dust, while their Donkey walks at his ease.”
paragraphs.zh: “看哪，”一个姑娘说，“瞧那两个傻瓜在尘土里跋涉，他们的驴子倒走得轻轻松松。”

paragraphs.en: The Man heard what they said, and put his boy on the Donkey’s back. They had not gone far before they came to some old men.
paragraphs.zh: 那人听见了她们的话，就把儿子放到驴背上。没走多远，他们又遇到几位老人。

paragraphs.en: “See here, now,” said one of them to the others, “this shows that what I said is true. Nowadays the young take no care of the old. See this boy riding while his poor old father has to walk by his side.”
paragraphs.zh: “瞧瞧吧，”一个老人对其他人说，“这正说明我说得对。如今年轻人不把老人放在心上。瞧这孩子骑着驴，可怜的老父亲却得在旁边走。”

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, the Man told his Son to get down, and he mounted the Donkey himself. In a little while they met three women with children in their arms.
paragraphs.zh: 听了这话，那人叫儿子下来，自己骑上了驴。过了一会儿，他们遇见三个抱着孩子的女人。

paragraphs.en: “For shame!” said the women. “How can you let that poor boy walk when he looks so tired, and you ride like a king?”
paragraphs.zh: “真丢人！”女人们说，“那孩子看上去那么累，你怎么能让他走路，自己倒像国王一样骑着？”

paragraphs.en: The Man then took the boy up behind him on the saddle, and they rode on to the town. Just before they got there, some young men stopped them and said:
paragraphs.zh: 那人于是把儿子也抱上鞍子，坐在自己身后，继续往镇上骑。快到镇上时，几个年轻人拦住他们说：

paragraphs.en: “One would not think so,” said they, “by the way you load him. You look more fit to carry him than he to carry you.”
paragraphs.zh: “看你们这样装货，可看不出来，”他们说，“你看着倒更像该扛着他，而不是他扛着你们。”

paragraphs.en: So the Man and the boy got off, tied the Donkey’s legs with a rope, fastened him to a pole, and, each taking one end of the pole, carried him along, while every one they met laughed outright.
paragraphs.zh: 于是那人和儿子下了驴，用绳子把驴腿捆起来，绑在一根杠子上，一人抬一头，扛着驴走，一路上遇见的人都哈哈大笑。

paragraphs.en: By and by they came to a bridge. Then the Donkey began to kick, and breaking the rope, fell into the water and was drowned.
paragraphs.zh: 走着走着，他们来到一座桥边。这时驴子开始踢腾，挣断绳子，掉进水里淹死了。

paragraphs.en: The old Man and his Son made their way home as best they could, thinking to themselves, “When we try to please everybody, we please nobody.”
paragraphs.zh: 老人和儿子只好尽力回家去，心里想着：“我们想让所有人满意，结果谁也没满意。”
